A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NSReg research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganisation.

before.justification: v2 reports original NSReg and baseline evaluations on six graph datasets, including ablations, data-efficiency experiments and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations involving T-Finance, DCI and GHRN, alongside further plugin comparisons.

M1.justification: The GraphSAGE backbone, three normal-oriented relation categories, relation fusion, joint anomaly-detection/NSR objective and inference procedure are retained. The separation into FE and FC and explicit linear-sigmoid predictor description provide additional specification; they do not establish an architectural or procedural redesign.

E1.justification: v3 adds the binary-labelled T-Finance graph, containing 39,357 nodes and 21,222,543 edges, with its anomalies divided into two subclasses for open-set evaluation. The six earlier datasets and underlying anomaly-detection task remain.

E2.justification: DCI and GHRN are added to the existing main benchmark, large-scale and data-efficiency comparisons, substantially expanding the graph-specific supervised competitors. The plugin comparison also expands from DevNet and BWGNN to include DCI. Earlier comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 explicitly specifies equal sampling of all three relation types. v2's statement about equal numbers of 'relation samples' and 'unconnected relation samples' leaves its proportions unclear, so a changed batch composition cannot reliably be distinguished from clarification. The class-rotation design, metrics and stated label budgets otherwise remain consistent.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 and Table 8 separately evaluate seen-anomaly detection, directly examining the fitting/generalisation tradeoff; this analysis is removed. The SAD, contrastive-learning, dual-relation and normal-anomaly ablations, sensitivity studies, data-efficiency experiments and runtime analysis remain, often relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random or independent runs and mean±standard-deviation results. v3's explanation of eight class rotations across five runs for CS clarifies the existing design rather than establishing more repetitions or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New T-Finance, DCI/GHRN and DCI+NSR results expand the tables and curves, while seen-only results disappear. Retained Table 1 entries are unchanged, but DCI becomes the second-best unseen AUC-ROC baseline at 0.681, making the retained 21% improvement claim approximately 18.6%. Some existing standard deviations change, including AMNet's ogbn-arxiv unseen AUC-ROC deviation from 0.009 to 0.053. v3 Table 8 also incorrectly copies AUC-ROC averages into its AUC-PR row, reporting NSReg as 0.849 instead of 0.622.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 1 in Section 3.3 and a contradiction proof in Appendix A; v2 contains no corresponding proposition or proof. The analysis introduces normal-subspace and boundary definitions, assumptions about a well-trained relation discriminator and homeomorphic transformations, and a conditional argument excluding anomaly regions enclosed within the normal region.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain open-set graph anomaly detection through normal-structure regularisation, improved unseen-anomaly generalisation and applicability as a plugin. v3's quantitative introduction claims summarise earlier reported gains; the additional datasets and competitors expand supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 connects the mechanism explanation to its conditional normal-subspace argument and adds an explicit one-hop limitation, discussing the sampling overhead of extending to more distant neighbours. It removes v2's discussion of the seen-anomaly fitting tradeoff and the qualification that additional seen-anomaly labels can reduce generalisation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the linear-sigmoid relation predictor, clarifies uniform normal-node sampling and relation-batch composition, and documents preprocessing for T-Finance. It omits v2's explicit 400-epoch, 0.001-learning-rate budget for the two ogbn datasets and the statement that plugin variants retain their original models' optimisation settings. These documentation changes do not establish changed implementations.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for GHRN, DCI and Generative Semi-supervised Graph Anomaly Detection, while removing the standalone Lloyd clustering and Deep Graph Infomax references despite retaining those preprocessing methods. Positioning relative to graph anomaly detection, supervised anomaly detection and imbalanced classification remains broadly unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganised from eleven numbered subsections into two principal subsections with introductory setup paragraphs. Runtime and hyperparameter discussions move to the appendix; training pseudocode moves from Appendix A to B, and Appendix A becomes the proof section. The abstract, introduction and method explanations are also extensively revised.

P2.justification: The two-column ACM layout becomes a predominantly single-column preprint with wrapped figures and tables. Figure 2 is redrawn, a proof diagram is added, and Figure 4 changes from a horizontal strip to a grid. Plugin, large-scale and ablation tables are expanded, split or relocated. The earlier hyperparameter overview disappears, but its detailed plots remain.

improvement.justification: The added T-Finance benchmark, DCI/GHRN comparisons and DCI plugin experiment provide broader empirical support for the retained generalisation and portability claims. The conditional theoretical analysis and explicit one-hop limitation clarify the rationale and scope. These gains are tempered by removal of the seen-only tradeoff evidence and some training details, plus incorrect appendix averages and an outdated comparative percentage, making the net improvement limited.
